record.paper_title: Open Problems in α Particle Condensation
record.original_question: Do linear α-chain states exist as physical nuclear cluster states, and if they do, are their α clusters arranged in quasi-rigid Brink configurations with fixed inter-cluster distances or delocalized along the line as one-dimensional condensate-like systems?

evidence.quote: However, this does not mean that the existence of linear alpha-chain structures is impossible. In fact, in the case of 12C, there are some reports that the third 0+ state around 10 MeV has 3α chain structure, although it is slightly bent away from the linear shape [19, 20]

The usual picture of the linear alpha-chain structure is expressed by the use of Brink wave function which has alpha clusters located on a line with equal inter-cluster distances. This means that Brink’s description assumes a quasi rigid body picture of the chain state.
From this knowledge, we can make the conjecture that the alpha clusters arranged on a line may move rather freely along the line instead of staying around some equilibrium points.

This result supports our conjecture that even in a linear configuration the α’s can preferably be in a condensate. In condensed matter such linear Bose condensates are called Tonks-Girardeau gases having quite particular properties [24, 25].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a self-conjugate (4N) atomic nucleus modeled as a system of N α-particles (α = ⁴He). A "linear α-chain state" is a nuclear state in which the α clusters are arranged along a one-dimensional axis. Two competing microscopic descriptions of such a state can be formulated:

(i) Brink-type quasi-rigid configuration: the many-body wave function is a Slater determinant of Gaussian α-cluster wave packets centered at fixed positions R₁, R₂, …, R_N located along a common axis with equal inter-cluster spacings, so that the α centers behave as a quasi-rigid one-dimensional crystal.

(ii) One-dimensional α-condensate configuration: the α clusters are delocalized along the line, all occupying (in the cluster sense) a common lowest single-particle orbital along the axis, forming a Bose-condensate-like state that, due to the strong short-range repulsion between α's, is expected to behave as a Tonks–Girardeau gas (impenetrable bosons in 1D, equivalent in density properties to a 1D Fermi gas).

Resolve the following questions:

(a) Do linear α-chain states exist as genuine physical eigenstates (resonances) of self-conjugate nuclei, in particular as excited 0⁺ states of ¹²C, ¹⁶O, ²⁰Ne, …, near or above the Nα threshold?

(b) If such states exist, determine which of the descriptions (i) or (ii) (or an interpolation between them) correctly characterizes the internal structure of the α clusters along the chain: are they quasi-rigidly localized at equilibrium positions with fixed inter-cluster distances, or are they delocalized along the line as a one-dimensional α-condensate of Tonks–Girardeau type?
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains an active research topic. Recent works (e.g., candidate linear-chain α clustering in ¹⁴C observed via Be-10 resonant scattering, and studies of the 5α condensate in ²⁰Ne) provide partial experimental and theoretical support for the existence of linear-chain and condensate-like α structures, but no consensus has been reached on whether physical linear α-chain states are best described as quasi-rigid Brink configurations or as delocalized Tonks–Girardeau-like 1D α condensates. The question is therefore still open.

status_evidence.title: One-dimensionality in atomic nuclei: A candidate for linear-chain α clustering in 14C
status_evidence.snippet: Evidence found through resonant elastic and inelastic α scattering for excited states in 14C consistent with linear-chain structure.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental candidates for linear α-chain states have been reported, supporting that the existence question is being actively investigated but not settled.

status_evidence.title: The 5α condensate state in 20Ne
status_evidence.snippet: Recent observation/analysis of an exotic 5α gas-like clustering state in 20Ne.
status_evidence.claim: α-condensate-like configurations are still being characterized experimentally, indicating the structural nature of multi-α states remains under active study.

status_evidence.title: Alpha clustering in nuclear astrophysics and topology
status_evidence.snippet: Review describing ongoing study of α-cluster gas-like and linear-chain configurations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reviews continue to treat the linear-chain vs. condensate description of α-chain states as an open structural question.
